newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed, bank leads gainers.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed, bank leads gainers.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed mixed in lackluster and mostly sideways trading in which Banco de Colombia was the only big winner, brokers said.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index shed 0.24 percent to close at 17,660.04 on a trading volume of about 3.7 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB rose a razor-thin 0.04 percent, meanwhile, ending at 1,168.03 on a volume of about 1.7 billion pesos.
Banco de Colombia, the second leading commercial bank in terms of assets, gained significantly a day after Santander Investment upgraded the stock from buy to "strong buy."
Santander said it cut its 1997 earnings per share estimate for the bank to $0.045 from $0.050, but raised its 1998 earnings estimate to $0.058 from $0.053.
Brokers said buying, mostly by foreign funds, pushed the bank's stock up 1.75 percent in Bogota to 405 pesos per share. It closed at the same level in Medellin, where it rose 1.76 percent.

Other gains included Carulla y Compania, Colombia's top supermarket chain. It closed up 0.84 percent in Bogota at 4,200 pesos per share on what broker's described as a tentative comeback from recent bouts of profit-taking.

Discount retailer Almacenes Exito also closed higher, buoyed at least in part by Tuesday's report its first quarter earnings were up 18.7 percent on last year. The stock added 0.55 percent in Bogota to end at 3,600 pesos per share.

But heavily traded blue-chips like Bavaria and Compania de Cementos Argos, the top cement maker belonging to the Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, closed unchanged and dealers said trading was mostly flat or sideways overall.
"There's still no definitive trend," one Bogota-based broker said. ((-- Javier Mozzo, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944))
